Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, OCTOBER 12,
2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. MAYOR PRO TEM SOLANKI PARTICIPATED VIA
TELECONFERENCE FROM THE SOFITEL PARIS LE FAUBOURG HOTEL, 15 RUE BOISSY
D’ANGLAS, PARIS, FRANCE, ROOM #642, AND THE MEETING AGENDA WAS BE POSTED AT
THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE .

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Juno Smalley, New Life Community Church.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 394.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki (via teleconference)
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Friends of the Cerritos Library (National Friends of Libraries Week).

 5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to approve Councilmember Vo’s
  nomination, as listed below, to fill an unscheduled vacancy of an unexpired two-year term
  of service expiring April 30, 2024 (COUNCIL):

  Nominee Name  Advisory Board
  Habib Ali  Community Safety Committee

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, October 12, 2023, 7:00 p.m.

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, administered the oath of office to newly appointed
  Community Safety Committee member Habib Ali.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Amir Greenidge inquired regarding the status of the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department ride-along program at the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station.

  Chris Kim, Commanding Officer, 1st Combat Engineer’s Battalion, United States Marine
  Corps, thanked the City and Friends of the 1st CEB Adoption Committee for their years of
  support.

  Marshall Cleveland, Battalion Sergeant Major, 1st Combat Engineer’s Battalion, United
  States Marine Corps, thanked the City and Friends of the 1st CEB Adoption Committee for
  their years of support.

  Charles Sooter, resident and member of the Friends of the 1st CEB Adoption Committee,
  provided a historical summary of the Committee’s activities and encouraged members of
  the community to consider joining the organization.

  Daisy Lagasca, member of the Friends of the 1st CEB Adoption Committee, encouraged
  members of the community to consider joining the organization and participate in their
  upcoming Golf Tournament fundraiser. She invited community members to attend the
  upcoming “Taste of the Region” Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce event.

  Alfred Reyes expressed his personal faith beliefs and noted his enthusiastic support of the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts, citing the strong community participation at recent
  performances. He also referenced the support the modernized performances provide to
  local businesses.

  Sam Desai, representing CerritosNewsPaper.com, requested news articles from the
  community and City for publication through his media outlet. He referred to the need for
  increased community participation and for the City to be aware of residents’ needs,
  especially during the holiday season. He submitted his business card as a document for the
  record. (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are considered public
  record. Public requests for copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence and/or
  photographs can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

  Thursday, September 28, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION (HELD PENDING): It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, to approve the
  addition of the Strategic Planning Session on Saturday, December 9, 2023 at the Cerritos
  Senior Center to the 2023 Cerritos public meeting schedule, pending modification of
  Cerritos Policy No. 2.04 (COUNCIL).

  The motion was held pending due to the following substitute motion:

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (PASSED): It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Barrows, to
  approve the addition of the Strategic Planning Session on Saturday, December 2, 2023, at
  a City facility to be determined pending confirmation of availability, to the 2023 Cerritos
  public meeting schedule, pending modification of Cerritos Policy No. 2.04 (COUNCIL).

  The substitute motion carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Barrows
  NOES:  Yokoyama, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  (The original motion died due to the vote taken on the substitute motion).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to direct staff to draft minor
  modifications to Policy No. 2.04 to allow for more flexibility in scheduling the Strategic
  Planning Session and present the revisions to the City Council for final review and
  consideration at a subsequent meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 0 – 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Yokoyama

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract for the printing of the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts 2023-2024 Calendar of Events, Bid No. 1522-23 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Vo, to award a contract to Southwest
  Offset Printing in the amount of $82,106.85 for printing of the Cerritos Center for the
  Performing Arts 2023-2024 Calendar of Events, Bid No. 1522-23. In the event issues of non-
  performance arise, the project would be removed from Southwest Offset Printing and taken to
  the next lowest bidder to ensure the City’s printing deadline, quality standards, and
  specifications are met (COUNCIL).

9C.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Sports Complex fencing refurbishment,
  Project No. 20106, Bid No. 1521-23* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,

  A staff report was given by Amandeep Mann, Associate Civil Engineer. A PowerPoint

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Johnson, to:

  1.  Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of
  the CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report

  2.  Award a contract to Everfence Corporation in the amount of $34,000 for Sports
  Complex fencing refurbishment (total bid), Bid No. 1521-23, and reject the other bids;
  and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows

12.  Closed Session (continued)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  ITEM 12A:

  Councilmembers Johnson and Vo were absent during this item and did not participate in
  the discussion or vote on this item.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Authorize the City to join as a co-plaintiff/co-petitioner in the case entitled City of Whittier et
  al. v. Superior Court of Los Angeles County et al., Los Angeles County Superior Court case
  no. 23 STCP 03579, transferred to Orange County Superior Court with the same case
  number. The complaint was filed by the City of Whittier and other cities in Los Angeles
  County challenging the Los Angeles County Superior Court’s recently adopted Misdemeanor
  and Felony Bail Schedules, with the case seeking declaratory and injunctive relief and/or
  writ of mandate to enjoin the implementation of the Bail Schedules. The substance of the
  case may be summarized as challenging what is commonly referred to a “zero-bail” or “no
  bail” system, and more specifically summarized as alleged in Paragraph 29 of the
  Complaint: “Defendants failed to satisfy their mandatory duties as to setting of bail”
  because the recently adopted Bail Schedules “impose a blanket lifting of whole swaths of
  categories from being bailable offenses, and requires only citation and release, or booking
  and release, as to blanket categories of offenses – with no detention or individualized
  evaluations or assessments of particular crimes or individuals”; and

  2. Authorize the law firm representing the City of Whittier and multiple city plaintiffs, Jones &
  Mayer, to serve as special counsel to the City of Cerritos as a co-plaintiff/co-petitioner in the
  litigation (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 0 – 2 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Johnson, Vo
  ABSTAIN:  None
